definition: In data mining, the WINEPI algorithm is an influential algorithm for episode mining, which helps discover the knowledge hidden in an event sequence.
details: WINEPI derives part of its name from the fact that it uses a sliding window to go through the event sequence. The outcome of the algorithm are episode rules describe temporal relationships between events and form an extension of association rules.

explainer.lead: WINEPI is an influential algorithm for episode mining, discovering knowledge hidden in an event sequence. It matters because it extends association rules to temporal relationships between events.

tiers.eli5: Imagine scanning a long log of events through a moving frame and noting which events keep appearing close together in time.
tiers.practitioner: It slides a window across an event sequence and outputs episode rules describing temporal relationships between events. A pitfall is that results depend on the chosen window width, which defines what counts as occurring together.
tiers.paperLevel: An episode-mining algorithm that uses a sliding window through the event sequence; its outcome is episode rules, an extension of association rules capturing temporal relationships. Limits stem from the window-based notion of co-occurrence.

explainer.example: In a log of sensor events, WINEPI finds a rule that one event type is typically followed by another within the sliding window.
